details:
Environment

    Headset: Meta Quest 3

    Streaming app: Virtual Desktop (latest public build, Wi-Fi 6E)

    PC: Windows 10 / 11, Steam version of VRChat

    Connection: Wireless (no Link cable)

Steps to reproduce

    Start Virtual Desktop on the Quest 3 and connect to the PC.

    Launch VRChat.

    Play normally.

    Remove the headset and leave it off for 3–5 minutes or longer.

    Put the headset back on.

    Result: Positional tracking is lost—the entire image now follows head movement.

    Exit VRChat through the normal menu.

    Attempt to relaunch VRChat from Steam.

    Result: No window opens; a background VRChat process remains and cannot be killed. Only a full PC reboot clears it.

Expected result

    After any headset removal, tracking should recenter and the scene should remain stationary.

    VRChat should relaunch without requiring a system reboot.

Actual result

    If the headset is left off for several minutes, positional tracking fails permanently for that session.

    A residual VRChat process prevents relaunch until the PC is restarted.

Work-arounds

    Keep headset removal under ~2 seconds, or reboot the PC after each session.

Impact

    Every long break forces a full system reboot, preventing quick re-entry or iterative testing.

Additional notes

    Issue does not occur with the standalone Quest (Android) build of VRChat; it is specific to PCVR over Virtual Desktop.

    Force-closing VRChat.exe in Task Manager leaves Steam showing the game as “running.” Only a reboot fully terminates it.
title: Tracking loss and unrecoverable VRChat process after several-minute headset removal when streaming via Virtual Desktop on Meta Quest 3
